claims.claim: Relation lookup is not intrinsically a new computational capability; under a substrate that already provides generic state access, key comparison, branching, and iteration, finite relation lookup is derivable as ordinary computation over stored data.
claims.scope: explicit S1 substrate contract and finite relation audit
limits: S1 generic state-readable contract is not yet the declared concrete contract of the current Machine substrate
the local executable audit is a minimal finite-map demonstration, not a universal proof
claims.next_discriminating_test: Specify the concrete Machine substrate's state-access primitives and determine whether S1 is actually satisfied.

claims.claim: Even when direct relation lookup is derivable from a generic substrate, a direct indexed lookup primitive can occupy a better resource point without expanding the underlying computable relation set.
claims.scope: minimal relation audit and universal-machine resource distinction
limits: the local cost model uses abstract ticks
real substrate cost depends on representation and hardware/runtime

claims.claim: The current abstract Machine model does not specify enough concrete state-access semantics to classify generic relation_lookup as already contained in the fixed substrate or as a new primitive.
evidence: repository audit of current abstract model
claims.next_discriminating_test: Declare and implement the minimal concrete state access contract used by the current interpreter core, then re-run the relation-lookup closure test.
